title: WCU theatre students stage Steve Martin's 'Bright Star' this weekend
summary: West Chester University's Department of Theatre & Dance is performing the bluegrass-flavored musical by Steve Martin and Edie Brickell in the Madeleine Wing Adler Theatre through Sunday, Oct. 18.
loc: Madeleine Wing Adler Theatre, West Chester University

title: Five projects win West Chester's 15th annual Preservation Awards
summary: The West Chester Downtown Foundation honored restorations including an 1883 home on N. Church St., a Dean St. twin converted back from apartments, and a carefully matched office addition at 220 W. Gay St.

title: West Chester Fire Department logs its busiest month on record
summary: The department answered 194 calls in September, the most in its 225-plus-year history, and is digging into a rise in false alarms. Good Fellowship Ambulance also reported Borough calls up 31% over last September.

title: West Goshen zoning rewrite could open the old Boston Market site to housing
summary: The proposed rewrite would move the 1.1-acre E. Gay St. property into a new Mixed Use Corridor district allowing apartments and mixed-use buildings by right. Supervisors are expected to take it up Oct. 20.

title: Chester County sheriff holds a one-day deputy hiring event Oct. 24
summary: Applicants can apply, take the fitness test at West Chester University and possibly interview in one morning, starting at the Justice Center on W. Market St. No prior law enforcement experience is needed; registration is required.
loc: Chester County Justice Center, 201 W. Market St., West Chester

title: Chadds Ford's historic Painter's Folly goes to auction Oct. 22
summary: The township is selling the 1857 Italianate house beside Brandywine Battlefield, once home to Howard Pyle's summer art school, after finding ADA upgrades too costly. Conservation and facade easements will protect it under any new owner.

title: Indoor pickleball chain behind Exton's Picklr club files for bankruptcy
summary: The Utah-based Picklr franchisor filed for Chapter 11 on Oct. 9, about two weeks after the operators of its Exton club filed their own petition. The company says all locations, Exton included, remain open while it reorganizes.

title: Borough Council weighs raising mayor and council pay to the state maximum, starting 2030
summary: An ordinance up for adoption Oct. 21 would set the mayor's and each council member's pay at $6,915 a year, the state maximum for a borough of West Chester's size. The raises would only apply to terms starting in 2030.
loc: Borough Hall, 401 E. Gay St., West Chester

title: Developer asks for more time on its 329-apartment plan across from Borough Hall
summary: The Michaels Organization wants an extension of the 2024 zoning relief for a seven-story apartment building at 5 N. Adams St. and seven neighboring parcels. The Zoning Hearing Board takes up the request Oct. 26.

title: Hoffman's Mill Dam is gone, and the Brandywine runs free through Chadds Ford
summary: The Brandywine Conservancy finished removing the 1800s dam just upstream of the Route 1 bridge after six years of planning, easing a flood choke point and opening the creek to paddlers and migrating shad. An accessible boat launch is planned for 2027.
loc: Brandywine Creek at Route 1, Chadds Ford
